# Independent adversarial/system verification

Verdict: CONDITIONAL. Full review found zero unresolved MATERIAL-CORE or MATERIAL-REMEDY contradictions in the corrected frozen four-file package. The proposal can qualify a safe system because acceptance, physical termination, independent dispatch authority and exact pending recovery remain explicit gates. It does not establish distributed durability today. BD-1 through BD-6 and M1 through M4 still block the offered deployment outcome; optional M5 remains conditional. The caller's bounded source-review exit test is met, with no runtime qualification inferred.

Reviewed spec.md, plan.md, evidence.json and plan-evidence.json. Revalidated all four corrected hashes in target-pin.json and all 14 dirty-source hashes independently. EV-35's disclosed tool/operation/query correction was reopened in both tables and both manifests; it now identifies reading a five-query capture. Spec and plan manifests have the same 41 source objects. Core prose was reviewed in full before that correction. First and corrected pins are retained in adversarial-source-identities.json.

Final bounded recheck: reopened P2-S after root explicitly added AS-5's stopped-workspace capture/removal acceptance condition. It requires independently readable bytes through sealing or qualified publication after complete writer quiescence before destructive removal with no mutation interval, and fails removal of the only bytes before verified publication. All four final hashes match target-pin.json; final plan SHA-256 is 1373e5dec887c0132a1c832e694d6b69fd4978955434ae2b1522f32966d11b0c. This adds no mechanism or runtime proof. Verdict and finding counts remain unchanged; actual successful Docs call count remains nine.

Isolation: fresh verifier context. Root synthesis, previous review reports/verdicts and the other verifier's findings were not read. Candidate research was used as source inventory, not verdict authority. No candidate edits, tests, model calls, installation, provisioning, provider fault injection or external contact occurred. This report and its own source inventory are the only authored files.

## Actual domain application and evidence

Successful Temporal Docs calls: **9**, independently discovered through ALL_TOOLS and called live. Exact queries, primary URLs and retrieved-content hashes appear in adversarial-source-identities.json. Live documentation is mutable corroboration. Repository source, immutable public commit sources and source pins supply the stable evidence layer.

Applied temporal:temporal-developer by reading its installed SKILL.md (frontmatter temporal-developer, version 0.6.2) and Python introduction, patterns, gotchas, AI patterns, external-storage and core gotchas references. Application covered deterministic Workflow versus Activity IO, handler completion, per-run versus application deduplication, cancellation versus physical death, replay versus effect retries, storage-driver maturity/retention and installed-version proof. Its ordinary retry recommendation does not override this contract's nonrepeatable effect and original pending attempt-one constraints. No native Claude Skill load is claimed; Claude-only proof-of-load is not proven for these Codex shell reads.

Atlas access used only repo-local wrappers. Read features/update/activities/feature.py, canary-go/update_with_start.go, sdk-python converter/_extstore.py and workflow/_handlers.py after discovery. They establish primitive precedent. Atlas SDK metadata is 1.32.0 while the reference lock selects Temporal Python 1.33.0; that index is not proof of the future installed deployment. Existing local .venv/lib locations were absent. This is a disclosed installed-source limitation, not a contradiction of a package that explicitly requires future installed provenance.

Primary external reads independently reopened pinned Mods declarations and sec-default registration, the October 1 announcement, Docker volume documentation, Kubernetes node shutdown guidance, AWS S3 conditional writes and Confidential Containers protected image storage. Vendor pages do not establish the actual selected filesystem or termination contract.

## Atomic claim ledger

| Claim and source anchor | Provenance | Verification | Decisive evidence and practical consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INV-1/plan Architecture: Worker loss ordinarily resumes the current execution; CAN deliberately changes RunId; logical intent excludes current attempt/RunId | product_constraint plus proposed_design | confirmed primitives; conditional composition | [Workflow identifiers](https://docs.temporal.io/workflow-execution/workflowid-runid#run-id), [Continue-As-New](https://docs.temporal.io/workflow-execution/continue-as-new), pinned _workflow.py replay state. Reset/retry are separate operations; stable application identity remains M1/M4 proof. |
| INV-3: model/filesystem/provider IO is Activity work; replay reuses accepted completion | product_constraint | confirmed | [Workflow replay](https://docs.temporal.io/workflows#how-workflow-replay-works), actual _workflow.py:580-652. Accepted orchestration is not a filesystem snapshot. |
| INV-5/A-60: accepted Temporal head plus exact immutable chunks can support SDK materialization without mandatory separate transcript SQL | proposed_design | conditional | [External Storage](https://docs.temporal.io/external-storage), converter/_extstore.py driver interface; _runner.py:396-457 and 580-592 require exact load/head/CAS. No source demonstrates this complete Claude adapter composition. |
| INV-5/A-61: cold bundle or reattachment preserves matching native state | proposed_design | conditional | FileSessionStore is append/load with local lock and no fsync; ProofStore is local SQLite. Docker volumes survive container removal but ordinarily live on the host. P2-S/P4/P6-S must supply backend/metadata/native evidence. |
| INV-5/A-62: separate entity schedules the original wrapper once and duplicate requests do not issue a spawn permit | proposed_design | conditional | [Entity Workflow](https://docs.temporal.io/design-patterns/entity-workflow#implementation), [handler deduplication](https://docs.temporal.io/handling-messages#message-handler-patterns), features and canary sources demonstrate Updates/Activity scheduling, not this cross-authority protocol. |
| INV-5/A-63: sealed manifests and exact orphan reconciliation prevent mixed accepted state | proposed_design | conditional | SDK guard checks accepted tail, actual Workflow accepts returned checkpoint before tool dispatch; no cross-system transaction exists in the inspected integration. P2/P2-S/P5 gate every write boundary. |
| INV-1/A-64: cancellation, expiry, deletion and detach are insufficient to authorize replacement | product_constraint and requirement_or_decision | confirmed distinction; conditional supervisor extension | [Cancellation](https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/workflow/cancellation-and-termination#cancellation), Kubernetes shutdown guidance and host_session.py:235-244,384-437. Actual supervisor refuses until checked termination/removal; distributed adapter remains unbuilt. |
| INV-4/A-66/A-68: application dedup and every live reference survive CAN/allowed recovery windows | proposed_design | conditional | Docs explicitly scope Update dedup to a run and require handlers to finish. [External storage lifecycle](https://docs.temporal.io/external-storage#lifecycle) requires retained referenced data. P8/P8-S cover tombstones, original IDs and references. |
| INV-7/A-65: effects cannot access authority/credentials or survive teardown | requirement_or_decision and proposed_design | conditional | Actual host admission is single-host/container source, not distributed physical proof; effect isolation and aliases require P7. Explicit codecs/failure conversion agree with [Failure Converter](https://docs.temporal.io/failure-converter) and [Search Attributes](https://docs.temporal.io/search-attribute). |
| Optional A-71 through A-74: observation, native projection and accepted response escrow are separate lanes | proposed_design/open_decision | conditional | Pinned declarations expose streaming turn.step, fallback after failed hook work and limited local store; current emitted production SDK API is unavailable. No optional implementation guarantee is claimed. |

## Adversarial findings and exact scoped qualification

These are outstanding acceptance obligations already represented in the package, not additional design defects. Each counterexample has a scoped anchor and mandatory basis. The required response is to retain and execute its existing gate after authorization, not adopt a newly invented remedy.

| ID / classification | Anchor, mandatory basis and concrete attack | Required evidence already owned by candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AS-1 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | A-60/A-63: ACKed exact state must survive the selected host-loss contract. Lose upload ACK, accept partial manifest, delete one accepted component or interrupt conditional result append. | M1 P2/P2-S and M2 P4/P5: same object/digest reconciliation, zero preacceptance effects, stale/conflicting UUID refusal; missing accepted bytes fail promised preservation rather than count parking as success. |
| AS-2 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | INV-4/A-68: current CAN run still points to old objects after old history/blob expiry; closed ID reuse could erase duplicate evidence. | P2-I/P8-S/P9-S: retain or reanchor all live/resettable references and dedup/tombstones, bound carry size, refuse expired/missing authority; BD-3 selects horizon. |
| AS-3 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | A-62: duplicate cached Update reply, new Update ID, reset outer attempt to one, replay original intent or reset/recreate ledger. Ordinary per-run dedup is insufficient. | P1/P1-T/P2-I/P8-S: one entity-owned scheduling decision and physical spawn, stable original key/digest, no caller permission reply, CAN carries intent, actual admin controls prohibit empty authority recreation. |
| AS-4 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | A-64/A-65: partition old host control while effect egress remains live; lost create/kill reply; surviving detached descendant; already-issued remote request accepted after death. | P3/P7: H2 remains denied until authoritative whole containment termination, immutable resource reconciliation, recorder distinguishes issuance time from later remote acceptance; uncertainty remains parked. |
| AS-5 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | A-61/A-63: workspace rollback removes file claims at unchanged generation; native Write/Edit metadata differs; mounted backend acknowledges without durable exclusive create/sync; destructive cleanup removes the only readable workspace before bundle publication. | P1/P2-S/P4/P6-S: independent intent survives rollback, race actual mount claims, exact opaque transcript plus metadata/postimages, escaping links/protected aliases refuse before SDK, physical acknowledged disk/host destruction. M1 protocol/P2-S and M2/P4 must prove stopped workspace remains independently readable through complete sealed publication, or qualified publication follows full writer quiescence before destructive removal with no mutation interval. Local SQLite/fsync assumptions are not production proof. |
| AS-6 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | A-66/A-67: late/conflicting signed answer, cancellation and CAN race, mixed SDK/CLI/package deployment. Exact pending identity and cancellation priority are required. | P6/P8/P9: one accepted decision, drain handlers, no cancelled continuation, old versions retained and replayed, mismatches refuse before startup/claims. |
| AS-7 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | A-71 through A-74: required hook disappears or throws after admission, direct plugin process/fs/http/MCP bypass, deny masquerades as suspension, incomplete provider stream masquerades as accepted response. | MG-0..MG-3, optional M2/M3/M4: independent native/direct capability controls, exact typed original pending proof, outer stream/raw prefix and provider counter; selected accepted response recovery issues no replacement request. Observation loss alone does not create this escrow requirement. |
| AS-8 ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION | A-70: old attested guest retains key, protected storage rolls back, replacement key release is mistaken for old guest death. | Optional M5: fresh authority/key epochs and stale guest tests plus M4 termination/intent rules; [protected image storage](https://confidentialcontainers.org/docs/features/protected-storage/confidential-image-storage/) explicitly lacks replay protection. |
| AS-9 OWNER-DECISION | BD-1 through BD-6: failure promises, substrate/owners, recovery horizon, load/deadlines, confidential threat model and adoption cannot be selected by this verifier. | M0 records actual owner answers. Until then implementation and deployment qualification remain blocked by the plan. |

Counts: MATERIAL-CORE 0; MATERIAL-REMEDY 0; OWNER-DECISION 1 grouped finding; ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION 8; NONMATERIAL 0; INCORRECT 0.

## Precedent classifications

- **sanctioned**: entity state through Updates plus main-loop CAN with handler completion; exact source [Entity Workflow pattern](https://docs.temporal.io/design-patterns/entity-workflow#implementation) and [message patterns](https://docs.temporal.io/handling-messages#message-handler-patterns).
- **sanctioned**: payload claim check / SDK External Storage as a payload transport primitive; exact source [External Storage](https://docs.temporal.io/external-storage) and atlas://code/sdk-python/temporalio/converter/_extstore.py.
- **partial**: separate Entity Workflow owning one wrapper scheduling decision with persistent logical effect dedup. Sources demonstrate Updates, state carry and Activity scheduling, not the candidate's accepted receipt/physical kill/reset boundary: atlas://code/features/features/update/activities/feature.py and atlas://code/canary-go/update_with_start.go.
- **partial**: accepted head plus immutable trajectory/workspace chunks with exact Claude conditional adapter. Claim check supplies references; _runner.py supplies expected-head/CAS recovery. Neither supplies their transactional acceptance composition.
- **partial**: downstream enforced idempotency and unique SQL/outbox intent. [Activity idempotency](https://docs.temporal.io/activity-definition#idempotency) establishes receiving-side obligation; no exactly-once arbitrary Bash precedent follows.
- **none_found**: complete original Claude pending recovery plus cold metadata bundle, independent nonrollback dispatch authority and authoritative physical handover. This bounded absence does not itself constitute a defect; the exact composition remains gated by M1-M4.

## Repository impact and phasing

Reference design-base HEAD and 14 dirty files are preserved. Confirmed feature/operational/security/test impact: _workflow.py policy dispatch currently raises PolicyExecutorUnavailable, _runner.py guarded SessionStore and original pending callback, _defer_hook.py policy deferral, _skill_package.py validated loading, host_session.py ownership/teardown, write_recovery.py exact result/postimage/admission paths and existing session_control tests. No change can safely bypass the policy refusal seam or attempt-one/fork guard.

Likely greenfield impact: durable SessionStore materializer/receipt schemas, entity or unique-store authority, bundle restore/seal publisher, independent supervisor backend, effect wrappers, gateway, codec/failure conversion, retention/GC/admin policy, Worker queues/deployments and observability. This is a transitive integration map, not invented deployed topology. FileSessionStore's local lock and unsynced append, ProofStore's local SQLite transaction and local daemon termination are useful bounded prior art only. The existing HostSession teardown verifies death and then removes the container; it supplies no workspace capture. Candidate INV-5's quiescent publication and proposed supervisor specialization must preserve independent readable stopped state until sealing. This is AS-5 qualification, not a claimed existing extraction guarantee.

Phasing is required because authority, persisted identities, storage, physical lifecycle, security and version compatibility cannot become safe in one atomic change. M0 decisions precede authorized M1 protocol/mutation evidence; M2 establishes actual two-host storage and terminal containment; M3 establishes actual compatible original pending/native recovery; M4 establishes security, retention, versioning, load and alerts. Optional M5 extends threat coverage. Stop conditions remain failed cleanup, uncertain intent/termination, mismatched state/version, open blocking decisions or failed acceptance. Rollback must retain claims/intent and compatible code; it cannot erase uncertainty or restore an empty authority. The proposed sequence and safe parked states are sufficient as a conditional design.

No deployment, runtime compatibility, vendor host-loss guarantee or installed distribution is verified by this source pass. The package's own explicit qualifications preserve those limits. Root owns final manifest/evidence gates and final verdict reconciliation.
